channel.title: Pier & Point · Smith Cardiovascular Research Building
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Smith Cardiovascular Research Building (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Smith Cardiovascular Research Building: The Smith Cardiovascular Research Building's size now leads with 232,000 sq ft, as a 2008 groundbreaking report and its contractors' own descriptions give it; its $254 million cost now cites that readable 2008 report.
item.description: The Smith Cardiovascular Research Building's size now leads with 232,000 sq ft, as a 2008 groundbreaking report and its contractors' own descriptions give it; its $254 million cost now cites that readable 2008 report. Source: https://www.industrialinfo.com/news/article/construction-begins-on-254-million-cardiovascular-research-institute-for-ucsf--132778; https://www.tutorperini.com/projects/education/ucsf-smith-cardiovascular-research-building/; https://www.rsconstruction.com/projects/education/ucsf-smith-cardiovascular-research-building/.

item.title: Correction · Smith Cardiovascular Research Building: The record gave 236,000 sq ft and $254 million from an Architizer listing that could not be read; two readable contractor pages give 323,000 sq ft and a $196 million contract amount, so the record now states the conflict instead of one figure. The September 2007 Regents minutes give about $180 million in gifts in hand but no project budget, so the $254 million clause was removed from that milestone. The opening is 2010 without a month (UCSF's history gives the year only), and the aerial photo caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'.

item.title: Planned · Smith Cardiovascular Research Building: UC Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings holds a preliminary design review of the Mission Bay Cardiovascular Research Building; the campus reports it is expecting a $100 million cash gift and a matching $50 million gift (bringing the campus close to $180 million in gifts in hand; the minutes give no project budget) and plans to seek full design approval in November 2007 (Sep 18, 2007)
